newsitem.title: USA: US corp debt issuers see window of opportunity.
newsitem.headline: US corp debt issuers see window of opportunity.

text.p: U.S. corporate debt issuers that had been sidelined by higher borrowing costs saw a window of opportunity Tuesday morning when Treasury yields dropped after weaker-than-expected economic data, dealers said.

Norwest Corp unit, Norwest Financial tapped the market unexpectedly Tuesday with a $150 million 10-year note deal which priced to yield 48 basis points over U.S. Treasuries. Merrill Lynch & Co served as lead underwriter.
"You'll probably see some market timers come in here...like Norwest did this morning," said one syndicate source.
"They take advantage of the runup in U.S. Treasuries and rates (yields) are 10 to 12 basis points lower than they were," the source added.

A lower-than-expected 0.6 percent rise in the first-quarter U.S. employment cost index and a 3.0 percent drop in March durable goods orders sent the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond up over a point and sent yields lower.
Late Tuesday morning, the T-bond was trading up 38/32 at 95-5/32 to yield 7.01 percent, compared with 7.11 percent at Monday's close.
Players feared that stronger-than-expected economic reports woud push the Fed's policy-setting arm, the Federal Open Market Committee, a step closer to hiking interest rates at its next meeting.
The FOMC, voted last month to raise the key overnight lending rate by 1/4 point, making it more costly for U.S. corporations to finance debt. Policy makers are set to meet once again on May 20.
Still, more economic data is on the way. They include Thursday's April NAPM report and first quarter GDP and U.S. nonfarm payrolls/unemployment data on Friday.
Turning to other new deals, American Brands issued $300 million in a two-part debt offering via JP Morgan Securities Inc.

The deal included $100 million in 20-year debentures to yield 85 basis points and $200 million in 40-year debentures, putable in 12 years, to yield 75 basis points over Treasuries, market sources said.
Among other upcoming offerings in the market are Briggs & Stratton Corp's $175 million five- and 10-year debt offering via Credit Suisse First Boston, sources said.
Sunlife Canada is also slated to bring $500 million of a step-up offering one day this week, sources said.
Dominion Resources is expected to issue $800 million in Baa1/A-minus rated debt offering consisting of five and 10-year debt via underwriter Lehman Brothers.
Meanwhile, CSX Corp is also slated to bring a $2.0 billion multi-tranche debt offering via underwriters Salomon Brothers, Credit Suisse First Boston and Chase Securities.
The deal is expected to include five-year, seven-year, 10-year and 30-year tranches, in addition to a 30-year trust preferred issue, sources said.
Price talk on CSX's deal is as follows, sources said.
-five-year seen at 55 basis points over Treasuries,
-seven-year seen at 65 basis points over Treasuries,
-10-year seen at 80 basis points over Treasuries,
-30-year seen at 105 basis points over Treasuries,
-30-year trust preferred at 155 basis points over Treasuries.
Looking ahead, Norfolk Southern Corp is expected to issue between $3.0 - $4.0 billion in a debt offering via joint lead managers Merrill Lynch and JP Morgan Securities.

Among upcoming high-yield issues, Pride Petroleum Services Inc is expected to sell $300 million in 10-year senior notes later this week via lead underwriter Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities. The issue has a three-year equity call for $100 million, sources said.
Colorado Prime Corp is expected to set $100 million in 10-year 144A senior notes via JP Morgan Securities.
Another $85 million in 10-year 144A notes is expected to come from HCC Industries Inc.
